feedbackWrong.false: Hebrews 2:17 begins with just that need.

cristologia-cam-cr-03-senhor-01.question: The exaltation in the text leads every knee to bend and every tongue to confess the lordship of Jesus.

cristologia-pro-cr-03-senhor-01.question: To confess that Jesus Christ is the Lord, according to the text, is for the glory of God the Father.

cristologia-sem-cr-03-senhor-01.question: God exalted him sovereignly and gave him the name which is above all name.
cristologia-sem-cr-03-senhor-01.learningObjective: Recognizing that God exalted Jesus with his name over every name; every tongue confesses Him Lord.

feedbackWrong.false: Read: God exalted him and gave him that name.

cristologia-cam-cr-boss-01.question: John 1:1, Hebrews 2:17 and Philippians 2:11 describe different people, not the same Jesus.
cristologia-cam-cr-boss-01.learningObjective: Articular who is Jesus: A Word that is God, a man who propitiates, a Lord who is confessed by every tongue.

cristologia-pro-cr-boss-01.question: The confession that Jesus is the Lord is sustained because the Word is God and man made propitiation.
cristologia-pro-cr-boss-01.learningObjective: Articular who is Jesus: A Word that is God, a man who propitiates, a Lord who is confessed by every tongue.
cristologia-pro-cr-boss-01.feedbackCorrect: Right: Deity, propitiation and landlords articulate.

cristologia-sem-cr-boss-01.question: The Word was God; he was made like the brethren; every tongue confesses that Jesus Christ is the Lord.
cristologia-sem-cr-boss-01.learningObjective: Articular who is Jesus: A Word that is God, a man who propitiates, a Lord who is confessed by every tongue.
cristologia-sem-cr-boss-01.feedbackCorrect: All right, the three texts say that.

feedbackWrong.false: John, Hebrews, and Philippians support these three phrases.

doutrina-de-deus-cam-dd-01-criador-01.question: Genesis 1:1 presents the world as something that is explained alone without a Creator.
doutrina-de-deus-cam-dd-01-criador-01.learningObjective: Recognizing that God is the Creator: in the beginning he creates heaven and earth, and the world is not explained alone.

feedbackWrong.true: The verse attributes heaven and earth to the action of God, not to chance.

doutrina-de-deus-pro-dd-01-criador-01.question: Genesis 1:1 puts God as the origin of heaven and earth, and not the world as the cause of himself.
doutrina-de-deus-pro-dd-01-criador-01.learningObjective: Recognizing that God is the Creator: in the beginning he creates heaven and earth, and the world is not explained alone.
doutrina-de-deus-pro-dd-01-criador-01.feedbackCorrect: Right: the verse founds creation in God, not chance.

feedbackWrong.false: This is the reading that the text supports: God creates in the beginning.

doutrina-de-deus-sem-dd-01-criador-01.question: In the beginning, God created heaven and earth.
doutrina-de-deus-sem-dd-01-criador-01.learningObjective: Recognizing that God is the Creator: in the beginning he creates heaven and earth, and the world is not explained alone.

feedbackWrong.false: Read the verse: God creates heaven and earth in the beginning.

doutrina-de-deus-sem-dd-01-criador-06.question: What does Genesis 1:1 communicate that links to this context?
doutrina-de-deus-sem-dd-01-criador-06.learningObjective: Recognizing that God is the Creator: in the beginning he creates heaven and earth, and the world is not explained alone.
doutrina-de-deus-sem-dd-01-criador-06.feedbackCorrect: Right: the verse presents God as Creator.

options.a: God is the Creator
options.b: The world explains itself

doutrina-de-deus-cam-dd-02-santo-01.learningObjective: Recognizing that God is holy: the trisagium fills the earth with glory, and holiness is his name.

feedbackWrong.true: The text binds the saint to the filling of the earth with glory.

doutrina-de-deus-pro-dd-02-santo-01.question: At Isaiah 6:3, holiness is no detail: it is the triple name of Jehovah, whose glory fills the earth.
doutrina-de-deus-pro-dd-02-santo-01.learningObjective: Recognizing that God is holy: the trisagium fills the earth with glory, and holiness is his name.

feedbackWrong.false: The text sustains holiness as central proclamation, not accessory.

doutrina-de-deus-sem-dd-02-santo-01.question: Holy, holy, holy is Jehovah of hosts; the whole earth is filled with his glory.
doutrina-de-deus-sem-dd-02-santo-01.learningObjective: Recognizing that God is holy: the trisagium fills the earth with glory, and holiness is his name.
doutrina-de-deus-sem-dd-02-santo-01.feedbackCorrect: Right: that is what the seraphim proclaim at Isaiah 6:3.

feedbackWrong.false: Trisagius and glory on earth are in the text itself.

doutrina-de-deus-sem-dd-02-santo-06.question: What does Isaiah 6:3 communicate that is linked to this context?
doutrina-de-deus-sem-dd-02-santo-06.learningObjective: Recognizing that God is holy: the trisagium fills the earth with glory, and holiness is his name.
doutrina-de-deus-sem-dd-02-santo-06.feedbackCorrect: Right: the trisagion places holiness at the center.

feedbackWrong.b: Repeating saint three times does not treat it as detail.
feedbackWrong.c: The whole earth is full of its glory.

doutrina-de-deus-cam-dd-03-trino-01.question: Matthew 28:19 uses the plural names for Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, as if they were three gods.
doutrina-de-deus-cam-dd-03-trino-01.learningObjective: Recognizing a God in three persons: baptism is in the name of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit.
doutrina-de-deus-cam-dd-03-trino-01.feedbackCorrect: Okay, the text says in the name, in the singular.

feedbackWrong.true: TB bears the name, not the names: one God, three people.

doutrina-de-deus-pro-dd-03-trino-01.question: Baptism in the name of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit points to one God in three persons.
doutrina-de-deus-pro-dd-03-trino-01.learningObjective: Recognizing a God in three persons: baptism is in the name of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit.
doutrina-de-deus-pro-dd-03-trino-01.feedbackCorrect: All right, one name, three people — the Trinity on dispatch.

feedbackWrong.false: This reading is sustainable by the singular name and triad.

doutrina-de-deus-sem-dd-03-trino-01.question: Jesus commands disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit.
doutrina-de-deus-sem-dd-03-trino-01.learningObjective: Recognizing a God in three persons: baptism is in the name of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit.

feedbackWrong.false: The verse brings disciples, nations, and the triune name.

doutrina-de-deus-cam-dd-boss-01.question: Creation, holiness and Trinity appear in the texts as loose themes, without the same God in the center.
doutrina-de-deus-cam-dd-boss-01.learningObjective: Gather creation, holiness and Trinity: the Creator is holy, triune and origin of heaven and earth.
doutrina-de-deus-cam-dd-boss-01.feedbackCorrect: Right: it is the same God — Creator, holy and triune.

feedbackWrong.true: The three axes describe the same Lord, not distinct gods.

doutrina-de-deus-pro-dd-boss-01.question: To know the Creator, according to these texts, is to confess him holy, triune and origin of heaven and earth.
doutrina-de-deus-pro-dd-boss-01.learningObjective: Gather creation, holiness and Trinity: the Creator is holy, triune and origin of heaven and earth.
doutrina-de-deus-pro-dd-boss-01.feedbackCorrect: Okay, this is the portrait the three stages support.

feedbackWrong.false: Creation, trisagio and baptismal name form this confession.

doutrina-de-deus-sem-dd-boss-01.question: The three texts state together that God creates, is holy and baptized in the name of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit.
doutrina-de-deus-sem-dd-boss-01.learningObjective: Gather creation, holiness and Trinity: the Creator is holy, triune and origin of heaven and earth.
doutrina-de-deus-sem-dd-boss-01.feedbackCorrect: Right: creation, trisagio and baptismal formula are in the texts.

feedbackWrong.false: Genesis, Isaiah, and Matthew bring exactly these three axes.

eclesiologia-cam-ec-01-corpo-01.question: We were all baptized into one body, whether Jews, Greeks, slaves, or free.

feedbackWrong.false: The text includes Jews, Greeks, slaves and free in the only body.

eclesiologia-pro-ec-01-corpo-01.question: The only Spirit forms two distinct bodies: a Jew and a Greek.
eclesiologia-pro-ec-01-corpo-01.learningObjective: Recognizing the church as one body in Christ: many members, one Spirit, Jews and Greeks at the same baptism.
eclesiologia-pro-ec-01-corpo-01.feedbackCorrect: Right: the text speaks of one body and one Spirit.

feedbackWrong.true: There are no two bodies: Jews and Greeks enter the same.

eclesiologia-sem-ec-01-corpo-01.question: The body is one and has many members; all, although many, constitute one body, so is Christ.
eclesiologia-sem-ec-01-corpo-01.learningObjective: Recognizing the church as one body in Christ: many members, one Spirit, Jews and Greeks at the same baptism.
eclesiologia-sem-ec-01-corpo-01.feedbackCorrect: Okay, one. Corinthians 12:12 affirms body one and Christ.

feedbackWrong.false: Read again: many members constitute one body, so is Christ.

eclesiologia-cam-ec-02-reuniao-01.question: The church of Acts 2:42 persevered only in doctrine, without communion, from the bread or prayers.

eclesiologia-pro-ec-02-reuniao-01.learningObjective: Realize that the church perseveres in the doctrine of the apostles, in communion, in breaking bread and prayers.
eclesiologia-pro-ec-02-reuniao-01.feedbackCorrect: Right: the verse describes this persistent life.

feedbackWrong.false: Acts 2:42 places all four in the same persevere.

eclesiologia-sem-ec-02-reuniao-01.question: They persevered in the apostles' doctrine and communion, in the breaking of bread and prayers.
eclesiologia-sem-ec-02-reuniao-01.learningObjective: Realize that the church perseveres in the doctrine of the apostles, in communion, in breaking bread and prayers.
eclesiologia-sem-ec-02-reuniao-01.feedbackCorrect: Okay. Acts 2:42 lists these four persistences.

feedbackWrong.false: Read Acts 2:42: doctrine, communion, bread, and prayers.

eclesiologia-cam-ec-03-missao-01.question: Besides baptizing, sending includes instructing the nations to observe all the things Jesus commanded.

eclesiologia-pro-ec-03-missao-01.feedbackCorrect: All right, dispatch and presence close together.

feedbackWrong.false: v. 20 unites teaching to 'I am with you until the end'.

eclesiologia-sem-ec-03-missao-01.learningObjective: Understand that the church is sent to make disciples of the nations, baptizing and teaching, with Jesus present to the end.
eclesiologia-sem-ec-03-missao-01.feedbackCorrect: Right: Matthew 28:19 states this sending and baptism.

feedbackWrong.false: Read again: disciples of all nations and trinitarian baptism.

eclesiologia-cam-ec-boss-01.question: Jews, Greeks, slaves and free in the same body coexist in these texts with common persistence and sending to nations.

eclesiologia-pro-ec-boss-01.question: The church is just a closed body, without ordinary perseverance and without sending it to the nations.
eclesiologia-pro-ec-boss-01.learningObjective: Articulate the people of Christ: a body in the Spirit, common life and mission to the nations.
eclesiologia-pro-ec-boss-01.feedbackCorrect: Right: texts unite body, common life and mission.

feedbackWrong.true: Acts 2:42 and Matthew 28:19 prevent this reduction.

eclesiologia-sem-ec-boss-01.question: We were baptized into one body; they persevered in doctrine, communion, bread, and prayers; make disciples of all nations.

feedbackWrong.false: The three passages support body, persistence, and nations.

feedbackWrong.true: They are asked by the look; Jesus will come.

escatologia-pro-es-01-volta-01.learningObjective: Recognizing that Jesus will return just as he was received in heaven; waiting is not looking empty.
escatologia-pro-es-01-volta-01.feedbackCorrect: Right: the text links this vision and the future coming.

feedbackWrong.false: The ‘thus it will come’ replicates the mode of the ascent seen.

escatologia-sem-es-01-volta-01.question: This Jesus will come the way you saw him go to heaven.

escatologia-sem-es-01-volta-01.feedbackCorrect: Okay. Acts 1:11 affirms the return in the same way as the ascent.

feedbackWrong.false: Reread: this Jesus will come just as you saw him go.

escatologia-pro-es-02-juizo-01.feedbackCorrect: Right: the text links attendance and moral retribution.

feedbackWrong.false: Each person receives according to what they practiced in the body.

escatologia-sem-es-02-juizo-01.question: We must all be discovered before the court of Christ.

escatologia-pro-es-03-novo-01.learningObjective: Recognizing that God will dwell with men; death, mourning and pain will pass away.
escatologia-pro-es-03-novo-01.feedbackCorrect: Right: divine dwelling and end of the first things.

feedbackWrong.false: God will be with them; the first things are passed.

escatologia-sem-es-03-novo-01.question: Behold, the tabernacle of God is with men, and he shall dwell with them.

feedbackWrong.true: Acts promises to return; Apocalypse, the end of death.

escatologia-pro-es-boss-01.learningObjective: Integrate the return of Jesus and the new creation: the one who ascended will return, and God will wipe out every tear.
escatologia-pro-es-boss-01.feedbackCorrect: Right: visible return and new creation hold together.

feedbackWrong.false: The texts combine the “so will come” and the tabernacle.

escatologia-sem-es-boss-01.question: This Jesus will come the way you saw him go to heaven, and God will wipe out every tear.
escatologia-sem-es-boss-01.learningObjective: Integrate the return of Jesus and the new creation: the one who ascended will return, and God will wipe out every tear.
escatologia-sem-es-boss-01.feedbackCorrect: Right: the two texts unite lap and final consolation.

feedbackWrong.false: Acts promises to return; Apocalypse, the wipe of the tear.

familia-cam-fm-01-alianca-01.question: The text tells a husband to love by the force of authority, not to mention the surrender of Christ.

familia-cam-fm-01-alianca-01.feedbackCorrect: Right: the model is the surrender of Christ, not the empty authority.

familia-pro-fm-01-alianca-01.question: The love of the husband, according to the text, imitates Christ's surrender by the church, not an empty power.
familia-pro-fm-01-alianca-01.learningObjective: Recognizing that a husband loves a woman as Christ loved the church: surrender, not empty rule.
familia-pro-fm-01-alianca-01.feedbackCorrect: Right: the meaning of the verse is surrender to the image of Christ.

feedbackWrong.false: The text measures the husband’s love for the surrender of Christ.

familia-sem-fm-01-alianca-01.question: Husbands must love their wives, as Christ also loved the church.
familia-sem-fm-01-alianca-01.learningObjective: Recognizing that a husband loves a woman as Christ loved the church: surrender, not empty rule.
familia-sem-fm-01-alianca-01.feedbackCorrect: Right: the text commands love as Christ loved the church.

feedbackWrong.false: Reread: the model is Christ’s love for the church.

feedbackWrong.false: Read Ephesians 6:1: obey in the Lord, for this is right.

familia-sem-fm-02-pais-filhos-06.question: What does Ephesians 6:1–4 communicate that binds to this context?

feedbackWrong.false: John shows public reading; Paul demands to know what is spoken.

linguas-originais-pro-lo-boss-01.question: The Word must remain in one language, so that the world does not understand it.
linguas-originais-pro-lo-boss-01.learningObjective: To relate the trilingual title of the cross with the call to an intelligible discourse.
linguas-originais-pro-lo-boss-01.feedbackCorrect: Okay, the trilingual title and clear speech point to being understood.

feedbackWrong.true: John shows three public languages; Paul requires intelligible discourse.

linguas-originais-sem-lo-boss-01.question: The title of the cross was written only in Latin, and Paul praises those who speak in the air.
linguas-originais-sem-lo-boss-01.learningObjective: To relate the trilingual title of the cross with the call to an intelligible discourse.
linguas-originais-sem-lo-boss-01.feedbackCorrect: Okay, the title has three languages, and speaking in the air is flaw, not praise.

feedbackWrong.true: John lists Hebrew, Latin and Greek; Paul condemns speaking in the air.

lucas-cam-lc-01-salvador-humilde-01.question: The angel's good news restricts enjoyment to a small group, excluding the rest of the people.
lucas-cam-lc-01-salvador-humilde-01.learningObjective: To go out knowing that the angel announces good news of great joy: a Saviour, Christ the Lord, was born in the city of David.
lucas-cam-lc-01-salvador-humilde-01.feedbackCorrect: Right, the joy will be for all the people.

feedbackWrong.true: The text says that the joy will be for all the people.

lucas-pro-lc-01-salvador-humilde-01.question: The announcement identifies the born as Savior, Christ the Lord, and not as a private hero of one clan.
lucas-pro-lc-01-salvador-humilde-01.learningObjective: To go out knowing that the angel announces good news of great joy: a Saviour, Christ the Lord, was born in the city of David.
lucas-pro-lc-01-salvador-humilde-01.feedbackCorrect: Right: Savior, Christ the Lord, for all the people.

feedbackWrong.false: The text unites Savior, Christ the Lord and all the people.

lucas-sem-lc-01-salvador-humilde-01.question: The angel says that today in the city of David was born a Savior, who is Christ the Lord.
lucas-sem-lc-01-salvador-humilde-01.learningObjective: To go out knowing that the angel announces good news of great joy: a Saviour, Christ the Lord, was born in the city of David.
lucas-sem-lc-01-salvador-humilde-01.feedbackCorrect: Right, the angel announces the Savior born in the city of David.

feedbackWrong.false: Read Luke 2:11: A Savior, Christ the Lord, was born.

lucas-cam-lc-02-misericordia-01.question: The joy of heaven is greater by the ninety-nine righteous than by the sinner who repents.
lucas-cam-lc-02-misericordia-01.learningObjective: To go out knowing that heaven rejoices more for a sinner who repents than for ninety - nine righteous.
lucas-cam-lc-02-misericordia-01.feedbackCorrect: Right, the greatest joy is for the sinner who repents.

feedbackWrong.true: Luke 15:7 reverses this: greater joy for what he repents.

lucas-pro-lc-02-misericordia-01.question: The text prepares you to see repentance of one as a motive for heavenly joy, not as insignificant loss.
lucas-pro-lc-02-misericordia-01.learningObjective: To go out knowing that heaven rejoices more for a sinner who repents than for ninety - nine righteous.
lucas-pro-lc-02-misericordia-01.feedbackCorrect: One who repents weighs heavily on the joy of heaven.

feedbackWrong.false: Luke 15:7 makes one repentant the center of joy.

lucas-sem-lc-02-misericordia-01.question: There will be greater joy in heaven for a sinner who repents than for ninety - nine righteous who need no repentance.
lucas-sem-lc-02-misericordia-01.learningObjective: To go out knowing that heaven rejoices more for a sinner who repents than for ninety - nine righteous.
lucas-sem-lc-02-misericordia-01.feedbackCorrect: Okay, the text compares joy exactly like this.

feedbackWrong.false: Read Luke 15:7: greater joy for a sinner who repents.

lucas-sem-lc-02-misericordia-03.question: According to Luke 15:7, where will there be greater joy for a repentant sinner?
lucas-sem-lc-02-misericordia-03.learningObjective: To go out knowing that heaven rejoices more for a sinner who repents than for ninety - nine righteous.
lucas-sem-lc-02-misericordia-03.feedbackCorrect: Okay, the greatest joy is in heaven.

feedbackWrong.a: The text places the joy in heaven, not in a court.
feedbackWrong.c: There's no talking about silence in the desert.
feedbackWrong.d: The comparison does not locate the joy in a palace.

options.a: In a court of righteousness on earth
options.b: In the sky
options.c: In a desert of silence
options.d: In a palace of Herod

lucas-cam-lc-03-caminho-jerusalem-01.question: The trip to Jerusalem appears in the text as a fluke, with no connection to being received into heaven.
lucas-cam-lc-03-caminho-jerusalem-01.learningObjective: Go out knowing that Jesus manifests a firm resolve to go to Jerusalem to be received into heaven.
lucas-cam-lc-03-caminho-jerusalem-01.feedbackCorrect: Okay, the days of being received into heaven frame the resolution.

feedbackWrong.true: Luke 9:51 links the sky's deadline to the resolution to go.

lucas-pro-lc-03-caminho-jerusalem-01.question: The reader is prepared to see Jerusalem as a destiny assumed to be received in heaven, not as an involuntary deviation.
lucas-pro-lc-03-caminho-jerusalem-01.learningObjective: Go out knowing that Jesus manifests a firm resolve to go to Jerusalem to be received into heaven.
lucas-pro-lc-03-caminho-jerusalem-01.feedbackCorrect: Right: the resolution expresses the meaning of the path.

feedbackWrong.false: Luke 9:51 presents Jerusalem as a resolution, not a chance.

lucas-sem-lc-03-caminho-jerusalem-01.question: Standing to complete the days when he was to be received into heaven, Jesus manifested the firm resolve to go to Jerusalem.
lucas-sem-lc-03-caminho-jerusalem-01.learningObjective: Go out knowing that Jesus manifests a firm resolve to go to Jerusalem to be received into heaven.
lucas-sem-lc-03-caminho-jerusalem-01.feedbackCorrect: Right: the text unites the sky's deadline and the resolution to go.

feedbackWrong.false: Read Luke 9:51: A firm resolution to go to Jerusalem.

lucas-cam-lc-04-vitoria-ressurreicao-01.question: The preaching in the name of Christ is restricted to one people and never begins in Jerusalem.
lucas-cam-lc-04-vitoria-ressurreicao-01.learningObjective: Letting go out knowing that the Christ suffers, let him rise again on the third day, and let him preach remission to all nations, beginning with Jerusalem.
lucas-cam-lc-04-vitoria-ressurreicao-01.feedbackCorrect: Right: it is to all nations, beginning with Jerusalem.

feedbackWrong.true: Luke 24:47: to all nations, beginning with Jerusalem.

lucas-pro-lc-04-vitoria-ressurreicao-01.question: The suffering and resurrection of the Christ substantiate the preaching of repentance for remission, and do not replace it with a mute triumph.
lucas-pro-lc-04-vitoria-ressurreicao-01.learningObjective: Letting go out knowing that the Christ suffers, let him rise again on the third day, and let him preach remission to all nations, beginning with Jerusalem.
lucas-pro-lc-04-vitoria-ressurreicao-01.feedbackCorrect: Right: the writing unites passion, resurrection, and preaching.

feedbackWrong.false: Luke 24:46–47 links the writing to the preaching in his name.

lucas-sem-lc-04-vitoria-ressurreicao-01.question: It is written that Christ should suffer and rise from the dead on the third day.
lucas-sem-lc-04-vitoria-ressurreicao-01.learningObjective: Letting go out knowing that the Christ suffers, let him rise again on the third day, and let him preach remission to all nations, beginning with Jerusalem.
lucas-sem-lc-04-vitoria-ressurreicao-01.feedbackCorrect: Right: suffering and resurrecting on the third day are written.

feedbackWrong.false: Read Luke 24:46: suffer and rise again on the third day.

lucas-cam-lc-boss-revisao-01.question: The Son of Man came only to observe the lost, neither seeking nor saving.
lucas-cam-lc-boss-revisao-01.learningObjective: To go out knowing that the Son of Man came to seek and save what had been lost — the thread of Luke.
lucas-cam-lc-boss-revisao-01.feedbackCorrect: Okay, the text unites seeking and saving.

feedbackWrong.true: Luke 19:10 says he came to seek and save, not just observe.

lucas-pro-lc-boss-revisao-01.question: Luke 19:10 summarizes the thread of the gospel: the Son of Man takes the initiative to seek and save the lost.
lucas-pro-lc-boss-revisao-01.learningObjective: To go out knowing that the Son of Man came to seek and save what had been lost — the thread of Luke.
lucas-pro-lc-boss-revisao-01.feedbackCorrect: Okay, the coming is a saving initiative, not a retreat.

feedbackWrong.false: The verse condenses to seek and save as a purpose of coming.

lucas-sem-lc-boss-revisao-01.question: The Son of Man came to seek and save what had been lost.
lucas-sem-lc-boss-revisao-01.learningObjective: To go out knowing that the Son of Man came to seek and save what had been lost — the thread of Luke.
lucas-sem-lc-boss-revisao-01.feedbackCorrect: All right, you've come to rescue the lost.

feedbackWrong.false: Read Luke 19:10: seek and save what was lost.

marcos-cam-mc-01-servo-autoridade-01.question: The announcement of Jesus in Galilee takes place while John still preaches in freedom.
marcos-cam-mc-01-servo-autoridade-01.learningObjective: Recognizing that Jesus proclaims the kingdom of God with authority: time has been fulfilled; one must repent and believe.
marcos-cam-mc-01-servo-autoridade-01.feedbackCorrect: Right: The text places the preaching after John’s arrest.

feedbackWrong.true: Mark 1:14 places the preaching after John is arrested.

marcos-pro-mc-01-servo-autoridade-01.question: The gospel preached by Jesus asks for an answer: repent and believe, because the kingdom is near.
marcos-pro-mc-01-servo-autoridade-01.learningObjective: Recognizing that Jesus proclaims the kingdom of God with authority: time has been fulfilled; one must repent and believe.
marcos-pro-mc-01-servo-autoridade-01.feedbackCorrect: Right: the announcement of the kingdom comes with a call to faith.

feedbackWrong.false: The text unites near kingdom and the double call: repent and believe.

marcos-sem-mc-01-servo-autoridade-01.question: After John was arrested, Jesus went to Galilee preaching the gospel of God.
marcos-sem-mc-01-servo-autoridade-01.learningObjective: Recognizing that Jesus proclaims the kingdom of God with authority: time has been fulfilled; one must repent and believe.
marcos-sem-mc-01-servo-autoridade-01.feedbackCorrect: Right: the text links the trip to Galilee to John’s prison.

feedbackWrong.false: Read Mark 1:14: Jesus goes to Galilee after John is arrested.

marcos-cam-mc-02-caminho-cruz-01.question: According to the text, anyone who wants to save his life will keep it, and the cross remains outside the following.
marcos-cam-mc-02-caminho-cruz-01.learningObjective: Realizing that following Jesus requires denying oneself, taking the cross and losing life for him and for the gospel.
marcos-cam-mc-02-caminho-cruz-01.feedbackCorrect: Right: whoever wants to save his life will lose it; the cross is part of following.

feedbackWrong.true: The text reverses this logic: saving life is losing it.

marcos-cam-mc-02-caminho-cruz-05.question: Complete the sentence: "For whoever wants to lose her life"
marcos-cam-mc-02-caminho-cruz-05.learningObjective: Realizing that following Jesus requires denying oneself, taking the cross and losing life for him and for the gospel.
marcos-cam-mc-02-caminho-cruz-05.feedbackCorrect: Okay, whoever wants to save their lives will lose her.

feedbackWrong.b: Losing appears in the second part of the paradox.
feedbackWrong.c: Following is the previous invitation, not this gap.

options.c: follow

marcos-pro-mc-02-caminho-cruz-01.question: In Mark's discipleship, the cross is no accident apart: whoever follows refuses and takes the cross.
marcos-pro-mc-02-caminho-cruz-01.learningObjective: Realizing that following Jesus requires denying oneself, taking the cross and losing life for him and for the gospel.
marcos-pro-mc-02-caminho-cruz-01.feedbackCorrect: Okay, deny yourself, cross and follow form one call.

feedbackWrong.false: The text unites to deny itself, take the cross and follow in the same invitation.

marcos-pro-mc-02-caminho-cruz-05.question: Complete the phrase: "Whom     your life for my sake and the gospel will save you"
marcos-pro-mc-02-caminho-cruz-05.learningObjective: Realizing that following Jesus requires denying oneself, taking the cross and losing life for him and for the gospel.
marcos-pro-mc-02-caminho-cruz-05.feedbackCorrect: Right, whoever loses his life for him and the gospel saves her.

feedbackWrong.b: Saving is the result, not the verb of this gap.
feedbackWrong.c: Deny yourself to appear in the previous call.

options.c: deny

marcos-sem-mc-02-caminho-cruz-01.question: Jesus calls the crowd with his disciples and teaches those who want to come after him.
marcos-sem-mc-02-caminho-cruz-01.learningObjective: Realizing that following Jesus requires denying oneself, taking the cross and losing life for him and for the gospel.
marcos-sem-mc-02-caminho-cruz-01.feedbackCorrect: Right: the call is to the crowd with the disciples.

feedbackWrong.false: Mark 8:34 begins with exactly this call.

marcos-cam-mc-03-cruz-ressurreicao-01.question: The announcement treats the crucified and the risen as two different people.
marcos-cam-mc-03-cruz-ressurreicao-01.learningObjective: To affirm that the crucified, Jesus the Nazarene, has risen and the tomb is empty.
marcos-cam-mc-03-cruz-ressurreicao-01.feedbackCorrect: Right: the same Jesus, the crucified Nazarene, is the one who has risen.

feedbackWrong.true: The text speaks of one: Jesus the Nazarene, who was crucified and rose again.

marcos-pro-mc-03-cruz-ressurreicao-01.question: The empty tomb confirms the victory of the Servant: the crucified one has risen and is not there.
marcos-pro-mc-03-cruz-ressurreicao-01.learningObjective: To affirm that the crucified, Jesus the Nazarene, has risen and the tomb is empty.
marcos-pro-mc-03-cruz-ressurreicao-01.feedbackCorrect: Right: Resurrection and empty place announce the victory of the Servant.

feedbackWrong.false: The text combines “he rose again” and “he is not here”.

marcos-sem-mc-03-cruz-ressurreicao-01.question: The messenger says they seek Jesus the Nazarene, who was crucified.
marcos-sem-mc-03-cruz-ressurreicao-01.learningObjective: To affirm that the crucified, Jesus the Nazarene, has risen and the tomb is empty.
marcos-sem-mc-03-cruz-ressurreicao-01.feedbackCorrect: Right: the text identifies the sought as the crucified Nazarene.

feedbackWrong.false: Mark 16:6 says just that.

marcos-cam-mc-boss-revisao-01.question: The text presents the Son of Man as one who came above all to receive honor from servants.
marcos-cam-mc-boss-revisao-01.learningObjective: Understanding that the authority of the Son of Man is to serve and give life as a ransom for many.
marcos-cam-mc-boss-revisao-01.feedbackCorrect: Okay, he's not here to be served, he's here to serve.

feedbackWrong.true: Mark 10:45 refuses "to be served" as purpose of coming.

marcos-pro-mc-boss-revisao-01.question: In Mark, the authority of the Son of Man is revealed in giving life as a ransom, not in being served.
marcos-pro-mc-boss-revisao-01.learningObjective: Understanding that the authority of the Son of Man is to serve and give life as a ransom for many.
marcos-pro-mc-boss-revisao-01.feedbackCorrect: Right: Serving and the ransom reveal the authority of the Servant.

feedbackWrong.false: The verse defines coming as serving and giving life as a ransom.

marcos-sem-mc-boss-revisao-01.question: The Son of Man came not to be served, but to serve.
marcos-sem-mc-boss-revisao-01.learningObjective: Understanding that the authority of the Son of Man is to serve and give life as a ransom for many.
marcos-sem-mc-boss-revisao-01.feedbackCorrect: Right: the text denies "being served" and states "serving".

feedbackWrong.false: Mark 10:45 says exactly that.

mateus-cam-mt-01-rei-prometido-01.question: The name Emmanuel, according to the text, means the sinless people.
mateus-cam-mt-01-rei-prometido-01.learningObjective: Recognizing that the son is called Jesus because he saves himself from sin, and Emmanuel — God with us.
mateus-cam-mt-01-rei-prometido-01.feedbackCorrect: Okay. Emanuel means God with us, not that.

feedbackWrong.true: Matthew 1:23 translates Emmanuel: God with us.

mateus-pro-mt-01-rei-prometido-01.question: The fulfillment of the prophecy presents the child as Emmanuel, that is, God with us.
mateus-pro-mt-01-rei-prometido-01.learningObjective: Recognizing that the son is called Jesus because he saves himself from sin, and Emmanuel — God with us.
mateus-pro-mt-01-rei-prometido-01.feedbackCorrect: Right: Emmanuel interprets God's presence in his son.

feedbackWrong.false: Matthew 1:23 translates Immanuel as God with us.

mateus-sem-mt-01-rei-prometido-01.question: The son will be called JESUS, because he will save his people from their sins.
mateus-sem-mt-01-rei-prometido-01.learningObjective: Recognizing that the son is called Jesus because he saves himself from sin, and Emmanuel — God with us.
mateus-sem-mt-01-rei-prometido-01.feedbackCorrect: Right: the name Jesus is bound to save from sin.

feedbackWrong.false: Reread Matthew 1:21: the name explains salvation.

mateus-cam-mt-02-reino-ensino-01.question: Those who weep are called blessed because they have been filled with justice.
mateus-cam-mt-02-reino-ensino-01.learningObjective: Realize that the Kingdom declares blessed the humble, the weeping, the meek, and those who hunger for righteousness.
mateus-cam-mt-02-reino-ensino-01.feedbackCorrect: Right: to those who cry the text promises comfort, not that phrase.

feedbackWrong.true: Matthew 5:4 promises comfort; plenty is 5:6.

mateus-pro-mt-02-reino-ensino-01.question: The beatitude of those who hunger and thirst for righteousness promises that they will be full.
mateus-pro-mt-02-reino-ensino-01.learningObjective: Realize that the Kingdom declares blessed the humble, the weeping, the meek, and those who hunger for righteousness.
mateus-pro-mt-02-reino-ensino-01.feedbackCorrect: True: the hunger for justice does not go unanswered.

feedbackWrong.false: Matthew 5:6 promises that they will be full.

mateus-sem-mt-02-reino-ensino-01.question: Blessed are the lowly of spirit, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.
mateus-sem-mt-02-reino-ensino-01.learningObjective: Realize that the Kingdom declares blessed the humble, the weeping, the meek, and those who hunger for righteousness.
mateus-sem-mt-02-reino-ensino-01.feedbackCorrect: Okay, this is the first beatitude of the passage.

feedbackWrong.false: Read Matthew 5:3: The kingdom is of the lowly of spirit.

mateus-cam-mt-03-autoridade-01.question: After reproof, the disciples claimed that the sea does not obey Jesus.
mateus-cam-mt-03-autoridade-01.learningObjective: Seeing that Jesus binds fear to little faith and soothes winds and sea, which obey him.
mateus-cam-mt-03-autoridade-01.feedbackCorrect: Right, they marvel because winds and sea obey.

feedbackWrong.true: Matthew 8:27 says that even winds and sea obey him.

mateus-pro-mt-03-autoridade-01.question: The wonder of the disciples recognizes that even the winds and the sea obey Jesus.
mateus-pro-mt-03-autoridade-01.learningObjective: Seeing that Jesus binds fear to little faith and soothes winds and sea, which obey him.
mateus-pro-mt-03-autoridade-01.feedbackCorrect: Right, their question confesses that obedience.

feedbackWrong.false: Matthew 8:27 states that winds and sea obey him.

mateus-pro-mt-03-autoridade-02.question: In Matthew 8:26–27, touch the missing word in "What man is this that even the winds and the sea to him    ?"
mateus-pro-mt-03-autoridade-02.learningObjective: Seeing that Jesus binds fear to little faith and soothes winds and sea, which obey him.
mateus-pro-mt-03-autoridade-02.feedbackCorrect: Exactly. Winds and sea obey you.

feedbackWrong.b: Reproved describes Jesus ’ action, not this gap.
feedbackWrong.c: Arise describes the gesture, not the verb of the disciples.

options.c: ♪ Standing up ♪

mateus-sem-mt-03-autoridade-01.question: When Jesus rose up, he rebuked the winds and the sea, and there was great calm.
mateus-sem-mt-03-autoridade-01.learningObjective: Seeing that Jesus binds fear to little faith and soothes winds and sea, which obey him.
mateus-sem-mt-03-autoridade-01.feedbackCorrect: Right: the text reports the rebuke and the calm.

feedbackWrong.false: Matthew 8:26 records exactly this action.

mateus-cam-mt-04-cruz-vitoria-01.question: Sending limits the disciples to one nation, without baptism or teaching.
mateus-cam-mt-04-cruz-vitoria-01.learningObjective: Understand that the resurrected was given all power, and he sends disciples remaining with them.
mateus-cam-mt-04-cruz-vitoria-01.feedbackCorrect: Right: the mandate is to all nations, baptizing and instructing.

feedbackWrong.true: Matthew 28:19–20 speaks of all nations and of teaching.

mateus-pro-mt-04-cruz-vitoria-01.question: The presence promised by Jesus lasts every day until the end of the world.
mateus-pro-mt-04-cruz-vitoria-01.learningObjective: Understand that the resurrected was given all power, and he sends disciples remaining with them.
mateus-pro-mt-04-cruz-vitoria-01.feedbackCorrect: All right, he promises to be with you until the end.

feedbackWrong.false: Matthew 28:20 says, Every day until the end of the world.

mateus-sem-mt-04-cruz-vitoria-01.question: Jesus was given all power in heaven and on earth.
mateus-sem-mt-04-cruz-vitoria-01.learningObjective: Understand that the resurrected was given all power, and he sends disciples remaining with them.
mateus-sem-mt-04-cruz-vitoria-01.feedbackCorrect: Right, he declares that he has been given all the power.

feedbackWrong.false: Matthew 28:18 states: All power has been given to me.

mateus-cam-mt-boss-revisao-01.question: Matthew 28:18 states that no power was given to Jesus in heaven.
mateus-cam-mt-boss-revisao-01.learningObjective: Join name Jesus who saves from sin with the power given to the resurrected.
mateus-cam-mt-boss-revisao-01.feedbackCorrect: Okay, the text says he's been given all the power.

feedbackWrong.true: Matthew 28:18: All power was given to me in heaven and on earth.

mateus-pro-mt-boss-revisao-01.question: The same Jesus who saves from sin declares that he has received all power in heaven and on earth.
mateus-pro-mt-boss-revisao-01.learningObjective: Join name Jesus who saves from sin with the power given to the resurrected.
mateus-pro-mt-boss-revisao-01.feedbackCorrect: Right: salvation and authority belong to the same King.

feedbackWrong.false: The two verses speak of the same Jesus.

mateus-sem-mt-boss-revisao-01.question: Jesus will save his people from their sins, and all power has been given to them in heaven and on earth.
mateus-sem-mt-boss-revisao-01.learningObjective: Join name Jesus who saves from sin with the power given to the resurrected.
mateus-sem-mt-boss-revisao-01.feedbackCorrect: Right: the two texts unite salvation and power.

feedbackWrong.false: Matthew 1:21 and 28:18 affirm salvation and power.

missao-cam-ms-01-comissao-01.question: Jesus first declares that he was given all power and then orders to go and make disciples.
missao-cam-ms-01-comissao-01.learningObjective: Recognizing that the commission is born of the power of Jesus: go, make disciples, baptize, teach — he is with you.
missao-cam-ms-01-comissao-01.feedbackCorrect: Right: the therefore links the sending to the power already given.

feedbackWrong.false: Go, for he follows the declaration of power in 28:18.

missao-pro-ms-01-comissao-01.question: The presence of Jesus until the end of the world sustains the mission; it does not dispense it.
missao-pro-ms-01-comissao-01.learningObjective: Recognizing that the commission is born of the power of Jesus: go, make disciples, baptize, teach — he is with you.
missao-pro-ms-01-comissao-01.feedbackCorrect: All right, I'm with you, don't cancel it.

feedbackWrong.false: 28:20 promises presence in the sending, I do not withdraw from the mission.

missao-sem-ms-01-comissao-01.question: I was given all the power in heaven and earth.
missao-sem-ms-01-comissao-01.learningObjective: Recognizing that the commission is born of the power of Jesus: go, make disciples, baptize, teach — he is with you.
missao-sem-ms-01-comissao-01.feedbackCorrect: Okay. Jesus declares this power before sending.

feedbackWrong.false: Read Matthew 28:18: the power was given him.

missao-cam-ms-02-testemunho-01.question: The power of the Spirit serves to be witnesses, beginning in Jerusalem and going to the ends.
missao-cam-ms-02-testemunho-01.learningObjective: Recognizing that the witnesses of Christ receive power from the Spirit: from Jerusalem to the ends of the earth.
missao-cam-ms-02-testemunho-01.feedbackCorrect: Okay, power, witnesses and a map that expands.

feedbackWrong.false: Acts 1:8 binds power, testimony, and geographical scope.

missao-pro-ms-02-testemunho-01.question: The witnesses of Christ are empowered by the Spirit, not by their own strength.
missao-pro-ms-02-testemunho-01.learningObjective: Recognizing that the witnesses of Christ receive power from the Spirit: from Jerusalem to the ends of the earth.
missao-pro-ms-02-testemunho-01.feedbackCorrect: Right: power descends with the Holy Spirit.

feedbackWrong.false: Acts 1:8 attributes power to the Spirit, not to self.

missao-sem-ms-02-testemunho-01.question: You will receive power as the Holy Spirit descends upon you.
missao-sem-ms-02-testemunho-01.learningObjective: Recognizing that the witnesses of Christ receive power from the Spirit: from Jerusalem to the ends of the earth.
missao-sem-ms-02-testemunho-01.feedbackCorrect: Right: power comes when the Holy Spirit descends.

feedbackWrong.false: Acts 1:8 states exactly this promise.

missao-cam-ms-03-discipular-01.question: The gospel must be delivered to faithful men who also teach others.
missao-cam-ms-03-discipular-01.learningObjective: Recognizing that discipleship is to deliver the gospel to faithful persons able to teach others — a chain of four generations.
missao-cam-ms-03-discipular-01.feedbackCorrect: Right. Faithfulness and ability to teach go together.
